title: Potted Shrimps
subtitle: Brown shrimps in spiced butter, set and served with toast
excerpt: Potted shrimps are one of the oldest British seafood dishes: brown shrimps warmed in spiced butter with mace and cayenne, then packed into pots and set until firm. They are served cold with hot toast. The butter carries all the flavour, and the shrimps must be the small, sweet brown variety , not prawns.
sourceNotes: Potted shrimps in the Morecambe Bay tradition use brown shrimps (Crangon crangon), caught in the shallow waters of Morecambe Bay and potted in spiced butter. The practice of potting fish and shellfish in butter dates to at least the seventeenth century as a method of preservation.

recipe.batchNotes: Make up to 5 days ahead and keep refrigerated. Bring to room temperature for 10 minutes before serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Must be made at least an hour ahead. Best made the day before.

glossaryTerms.definition: Butter with the milk solids and water removed by gentle melting and skimming, leaving pure butterfat. It keeps longer than whole butter and is used to seal potted dishes.

content.text: Potted shrimps take about 10 minutes to make and need only an hour to set. The spiced butter is the key: mace and cayenne must be assertive enough to cut through the richness. Brown shrimps are tiny and intensely flavoured; if you can only get larger cooked prawns, chop them and reduce the spice slightly.

items.prepNote: peeled weight of cooked brown shrimps

content.text: Melt {{unsalted-butter}} of butter in a small pan over low heat. Add the mace and cayenne and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the shrimps and warm gently for 2 minutes; do not boil. Squeeze in the lemon juice and season with a pinch of salt. Taste and adjust the spice.

Spoon the shrimps with about two-thirds of the butter into 4 small pots or ramekins. Leave the remaining butter in the pan and let it settle: the milk solids will sink. Pour the clear top layer, which is now
, over the pots to seal. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour until set.
Serve cold, directly from the pot, with hot toast.

items.symptom: The butter seal has cracked or pulled away from the pot
items.cause: The butter was poured in too thick a layer, or the pot was very cold.
items.fix: Pour the sealing butter in a thin, even layer. If it cracks, melt a little extra butter and pour over to fill the gap.

items.cause: They were cooked too long in the butter.
items.fix: Brown shrimps are already cooked. They only need warming through in the spiced butter, not cooking again. 2 minutes over gentle heat is plenty.

items.cause: The spices were insufficient or the lemon was omitted.
items.fix: The mace and cayenne should be clearly detectable. Add more if the mixture tastes only of butter. The lemon is essential for balance.

items.symptom: The potted shrimps are watery when turned out
items.cause: The shrimps released liquid during storage.
items.fix: Pat the shrimps dry before using if they have been in brine. Pour off any liquid that accumulates before sealing with butter.

content.text: Morecambe Bay potted shrimps are one of the few British seafood dishes to have become internationally celebrated. The tiny brown shrimps from the bay were historically carried to London by horse-drawn cart, potted in butter along the way. They appear on the menus of classic London restaurants and hotel dining rooms as a starter that combines simplicity and luxury in the same small pot.
